brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Built on 2 bases (piece:0,0,0;full and piece:1,0,0;full) with two full-depth bins (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) holding fork/spoon props to demonstrate use.
The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it does not verify materials, sealing, waterproofing. Parts are 3D-printed in user-chosen material and layer lines are not water-tight as modelled.
Heat, water, detergent resistance and food safety depend on filament choice and print settings, which the configurator cannot verify. Cannot claim dishwasher safety.

finish.summary: Built a compact two-bin utensil holder (two adjacent cells with full-depth bins). Demonstrated with utensil props. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe claims are not verifiable in Hex Cluster – shape helps contain items but material/heat/food safety remains unmet and depends on filament the user prints with.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
